newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia's Zastava has problems with home sales.
newsitem.headline: Serbia's Zastava has problems with home sales.

text.p: Serbia's only car producer Zastava said on Tuesday illegal imports of second-hand cars were threatening its position on the local market.
"Sales on the domestic market are seriously jeopardised by the uncontrolled import of second-hand cars," Slobodan Radovic, Zastava Group commercial director, told reporters.

Some 100,000 second-hand cars are believed to have entered the country over the past eight months using a loophole in the law allowing registration of vehicles from the former Yugoslav republics without payment of customs duties.
Cheaper second-hand cars despite age and mileage are more attractive to the domestic buyer than the new basic models produced by the only local car maker Zastava, traders say.
Legislation allowing registration of second-hand cars expired in Serbia several months ago but is still in force in Montenegro until May 15.
Customs duties on imported cars are around 44 percent as opposed to one percent paid on cars from other former Yugoslav republics.
Radovic said the imported vehicles met the purchasing power of the segment of the population which was targeted by Zastava cars.
"This is a factor which significantly influences our sales capacities because it is a dumping of sorts. It is important for the process to end," Radovic said.

Even if imports end on May 15, when the law expires, consequences on the domestic market will not be visible until later because many cars have still not found their final buyer and are circulating at different car markets, he said.
Under a production programme agreed with the Serbian government Zastava cars will produce 23,000 units by the end of 1997, 10,000 of which were to be sold abroad and the rest on the domestic market.
"We think export plans are realistic, it is the domestic sales that pose a problem," Radovic said.
In the first four months this year Zastava produced and sold 1,900 cars and plans to produce 2,100 in May, he said.
Zastava has exported some 600 cars so far. In May it will export another 720 cars to Egypt and send the first shipment of 100 cars to the Czech Republic.
Zastava also plans to export 150 cars to Macedonia this month and is ending negotiations on exports to Slovenia and Poland.

Zastava produced nearly 200,000 cars in 1990 before the breakup of the former Yugoslavia and expects to produce 150,000 cars by the year 2001 if it finds a joint venture partner. -- Beti Bilandzic, Belgrade newsroom 381 11 222 43 05
